recognize_zh: 許多紅血球失去中央淡染區、呈緻密小圓形，表面伸出數量不一、長短與間距不規則的尖刺突起，這就是棘狀紅血球（acanthocyte），在嬰兒要想到無β脂蛋白血症。
features: Numerous acanthocytes: dense, spheroidal red cells lacking central pallor with 2–10 irregularly spaced spicules of variable length
Some cells with more regular crenation resembling echinocytes admixed
Remaining red cells normocytic with preserved central pallor
Platelets present, no schistocytes or red cell agglutination
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a prominent population of acanthocytes, which are small dense red cells without central pallor bearing irregularly spaced projections of unequal length. The remaining red cells are largely normocytic and normochromic, with a few polychromatic cells indicating reticulocytosis. Platelets are present and leukocytes are not seen in this field. Findings are consistent with acanthocytosis, which in an infant with failure to thrive and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency suggests abetalipoproteinemia.

ddx.vs: Echinocytes have 10–30 short, evenly spaced blunt projections around a cell that retains its size and often central pallor, whereas acanthocytes have fewer irregular spicules on a dense cell.

ddx.dx: Spur cell anemia of severe liver disease
ddx.vs: Spur cells are morphologically similar acanthocytes, so separation relies on clinical context and lipid studies (absent apoB/LDL in abetalipoproteinemia).
These show similar acanthocytes but normal lipoproteins; McLeod is identified by weak Kell antigens and XK gene testing.
PK deficiency shows prickle-cell echinocytes with enzyme deficiency on assay, not hypolipidemia.
